questions.prompt: Which item is a common cause of fire outbreaks in a school workshop?
questions.correctAnswer: An overloaded electrical socket
questions.explanation: Overloaded sockets can overheat and start fires, especially where cables or plugs are damaged.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify possible causes of fire outbreaks in the environment.

questions.prompt: Which group contains materials that can burn easily if handled carelessly?
questions.correctAnswer: Paper, sawdust, and petrol
questions.explanation: Paper, sawdust, and petrol are combustible or flammable materials, so they need careful storage and handling.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise combustible and flammable materials in the work environment.

questions.prompt: Which practice best prevents fire caused by electrical faults?
options: Report damaged cables and avoid overloading sockets
questions.correctAnswer: Report damaged cables and avoid overloading sockets
questions.explanation: Reporting faults and using sockets correctly reduces overheating, short circuits, and electric shock risk.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain ways of preventing fire outbreaks in the environment.

questions.prompt: Which three conditions are usually needed for a fire to continue burning?
questions.correctAnswer: Fuel, heat, and oxygen
questions.explanation: Fire needs fuel, heat, and oxygen; removing one of them can help extinguish the fire.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain basic conditions that allow fire to burn.

questions.prompt: A small flame starts on dry paper in a metal tray during a demonstration. Which method shows smothering?
options: Covering it with a fire blanket to cut off oxygen
Adding more paper to the flame
questions.correctAnswer: Covering it with a fire blanket to cut off oxygen
questions.explanation: Smothering puts out fire by limiting oxygen, which is one of the things fire needs to continue burning.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply appropriate firefighting techniques to simple fire situations.

questions.prompt: Why should learners avoid pouring water on a suspected electrical fire?
options: Water can conduct electricity and increase shock risk
Water always makes electrical fires brighter
questions.correctAnswer: Water can conduct electricity and increase shock risk
questions.explanation: Water may conduct electricity, so electrical fires require the correct extinguisher and adult guidance.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse safe and unsafe responses to different fire hazards.

questions.prompt: A class is preparing a workshop fire-safety plan. Which action should be included first?
options: Mark clear exits, assembly points, equipment positions, and reporting steps
Store all waste near the door for quick collection
Let each learner decide a different alarm signal
Keep firefighting equipment locked in an unknown room
questions.correctAnswer: Mark clear exits, assembly points, equipment positions, and reporting steps
questions.explanation: A practical plan shows how people leave safely, where they assemble, and how hazards are reported.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan safe actions for preventing and responding to fire outbreaks.

questions.prompt: In an electronic device, what is data?
options: Facts or values stored or processed by the device
Only the plastic case of the device
questions.correctAnswer: Facts or values stored or processed by the device
questions.explanation: Data is raw facts such as names, marks, pictures, or numbers that a device can store or process.
questions.learningOutcome: Outline the meaning and importance of data in an electronic device.

questions.prompt: Which example is a threat to data safety?
options: A computer virus that damages files
A labelled folder on a desktop
questions.correctAnswer: A computer virus that damages files
questions.explanation: Viruses can corrupt, delete, or expose data, so devices need safe use and protective software.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify threats to data in an electronic device.

questions.prompt: Which password habit best protects a learner's project files?
options: Use a strong private password and keep it secret
Use the word password for every account
Share the password with the whole class
Write the password on the monitor
questions.correctAnswer: Use a strong private password and keep it secret
questions.explanation: A strong private password reduces the chance of unauthorised access to files and accounts.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe ways of protecting data in an electronic device.

questions.prompt: Why should antivirus software be updated regularly?
options: To help detect newer threats that can harm data
To change every file into a picture
To stop the screen from displaying text
questions.correctAnswer: To help detect newer threats that can harm data
questions.explanation: Updates help antivirus software recognise and block newer viruses and other malicious programs.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain techniques used to secure data in electronic devices.

questions.prompt: A learner stores a copy of a design file on a flash drive and another copy in a safe school folder. Which data-safety practice is shown?
questions.correctAnswer: Backing up files
questions.explanation: A backup is an extra copy that can help recover work if the original file is lost or damaged.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply backup practices to protect electronic data.

questions.prompt: A message asks a learner to click a strange link and enter a password to win a phone. What is the safest response?
options: Do not click it and report it to the teacher
Click it quickly before time ends
Enter the password to test it
questions.correctAnswer: Do not click it and report it to the teacher
questions.explanation: Suspicious links can be used to steal passwords or install harmful software, so they should be reported.
questions.learningOutcome: Secure data by responding safely to suspicious digital messages.

questions.prompt: Which situation creates the highest risk of unauthorised access to a school computer account?
options: Leaving the account signed in on a shared computer
Saving work in a named folder
Closing a drawing application after use
questions.correctAnswer: Leaving the account signed in on a shared computer
questions.explanation: If an account remains signed in, another user may open, change, or copy files without permission.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse user habits that expose data to unauthorised access.

questions.prompt: Which plan best protects digital project files throughout a term?
options: Use strong passwords, scan storage devices, make backups, and sign out after use
Use one shared password and keep files only on one device
Disable antivirus so files open faster
Save every file with the same name and never back up
questions.correctAnswer: Use strong passwords, scan storage devices, make backups, and sign out after use
questions.explanation: A good data-safety plan combines access control, malware protection, backups, and responsible account use.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a simple plan for protecting electronic data from common threats.

questions.prompt: Which instrument is used to draw and measure angles in plane geometry?
questions.correctAnswer: Protractor
questions.explanation: A protractor is a drawing instrument used to measure and draw angles accurately.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify instruments used in drawing.

questions.prompt: Which set best describes a proper drawing environment?
options: Flat drawing surface, clean paper, margins, and title block
Rough floor, wet paper, and loose nails
Dark room, torn paper, and no measuring tools
Crowded bench with food and drinks
questions.correctAnswer: Flat drawing surface, clean paper, margins, and title block
questions.explanation: A well-arranged drawing environment supports neat, accurate, and easy-to-read technical drawings.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the layout of a drawing environment.

questions.prompt: What is a combined shape in technical drawing?
options: A figure made by joining two or more simple shapes
A random stain on drawing paper
A tool used only for cutting timber
A password for a drawing file
questions.correctAnswer: A figure made by joining two or more simple shapes
questions.explanation: Combined shapes are made from basic shapes such as rectangles, triangles, circles, and semicircles.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain combined shapes applied in drawing.

questions.prompt: Which drawing tool is most suitable for constructing a circle?
questions.correctAnswer: Compass
questions.explanation: A compass holds a fixed radius and rotates around a centre point to draw a circle.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify instruments used to construct plane figures.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to construct a rectangle joined to a semicircle to design a simple gate sign. Which skill is being applied?
questions.correctAnswer: Constructing combined shapes
questions.explanation: Joining a rectangle and a semicircle uses plane geometry to form a combined shape for a design.
questions.learningOutcome: Construct combined shapes applied in drawing.

questions.prompt: A drawing has straight edges, arcs, and equal repeated shapes for a window grille. Why is plane geometry useful here?
options: It helps arrange accurate shapes that can be made from materials
It removes the need for measurement
questions.correctAnswer: It helps arrange accurate shapes that can be made from materials
questions.explanation: Plane geometry helps designers construct accurate shapes that can guide production work.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how combined shapes are applied in day-to-day designs.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of dimensioning a technical drawing?
options: To show the sizes and positions needed to make the object
To decorate the drawing with random numbers
To hide measurements from the maker
questions.correctAnswer: To show the sizes and positions needed to make the object
questions.explanation: Dimensioning gives measurements so that a part can be made or checked accurately.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of dimensioning in drawing.

questions.prompt: Which type of dimension shows the size of an angle?
questions.correctAnswer: Angular dimension
questions.explanation: Angular dimensions show angle measurements, usually in degrees.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify types of dimensioning in drawing.

questions.prompt: Which line usually carries the numerical measurement in a dimensioned drawing?
questions.correctAnswer: Dimension line
questions.explanation: A dimension line shows the direction and extent of a measurement and carries the dimension value.
questions.learningOutcome: Draw and interpret lines used for dimensioning.

questions.prompt: A learner marks three connected lengths one after another along the same edge of a drawing. Which form of dimensioning is being used?
questions.correctAnswer: Chain dimensioning
questions.explanation: Chain dimensioning places consecutive measurements end to end along a feature.
questions.learningOutcome: Use forms of dimensioning to dimension given shapes.

questions.prompt: Which dimensioning form places several measurements from the same baseline or reference edge?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallel dimensioning
questions.explanation: Parallel dimensioning uses one reference edge, helping reduce accumulated measurement errors.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply parallel dimensioning to simple technical drawings.

questions.prompt: A drawing of a shelf bracket lacks the hole diameter. What problem is most likely during production?
options: The maker may drill a hole of the wrong size
The bracket will automatically fit better
The drawing will need fewer tools
The material will become lighter by itself
questions.correctAnswer: The maker may drill a hole of the wrong size
questions.explanation: Missing dimensions can lead to incorrect sizes, wasted material, and parts that do not fit.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse the effect of missing dimensions in technical drawings.

questions.prompt: A learner must prepare a neat drawing of a simple phone stand for making. Which dimensioning plan is best?
options: Show overall size, slot width, hole positions, and clear units without repeating unnecessary dimensions
Write random sizes beside every empty space
Leave all sizes for the maker to guess
Use only colour shading instead of measurements
questions.correctAnswer: Show overall size, slot width, hole positions, and clear units without repeating unnecessary dimensions
questions.explanation: Good dimensioning gives the maker enough clear information while avoiding confusion and duplication.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a dimensioning plan for a simple technical drawing.

questions.prompt: What does a plain scale show in technical drawing?
options: The relationship between drawing size and actual size
The colour of a ceramic item
questions.correctAnswer: The relationship between drawing size and actual size
questions.explanation: A plain scale helps represent real measurements on paper in a reduced or enlarged form.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the features of a plain scale used in drawing.

questions.prompt: In a scale of 1:2, what does 1 cm on the drawing represent?
questions.correctAnswer: 2 cm on the actual object
questions.explanation: A 1:2 scale means one unit on the drawing represents two equal units on the actual object.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret a plain scale used in drawing.

questions.prompt: A 20 cm object is drawn using a scale of 1:2. What length should appear on the drawing?
questions.correctAnswer: 10 cm
questions.explanation: At a 1:2 scale, the drawing is half the actual size, so 20 cm becomes 10 cm.
questions.learningOutcome: Draw plane figures to a given scale.

questions.prompt: A line is 5 cm long on a drawing made to a scale of 1:4. What is the actual length?
questions.correctAnswer: 20 cm
questions.explanation: At 1:4 scale, actual length is four times the drawing length, so 5 cm times 4 equals 20 cm.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret measurements from a plain scale drawing.

questions.prompt: Why are large objects often drawn to a reduced scale?
options: So the drawing can fit on paper while keeping correct proportions
questions.correctAnswer: So the drawing can fit on paper while keeping correct proportions
questions.explanation: Reduced scale drawings allow large objects to be represented clearly on available paper.
questions.learningOutcome: Appreciate the use of plain scale drawing in the work environment.

questions.prompt: A 120 cm bench top must be shown on an A4 page. Which choice is most reasonable before drawing?
options: Choose a suitable reduced scale and label it clearly
Draw the bench at full size across several desks
Guess a short line without writing the scale
questions.correctAnswer: Choose a suitable reduced scale and label it clearly
questions.explanation: A suitable scale keeps the drawing manageable and allows another person to interpret the real size.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse scale choices for drawing plane figures in a work environment.

questions.prompt: What is visual programming?
options: Creating instructions by arranging blocks or visual elements
Typing only random numbers into a calculator
questions.correctAnswer: Creating instructions by arranging blocks or visual elements
questions.explanation: Visual programming uses blocks, icons, or other visual elements to build instructions for a computer.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify visual programming applications used in day-to-day life.

questions.prompt: In visual programming, why is the order of blocks important?
options: The program follows instructions in sequence
The computer ignores all block positions
Order matters only in printed posters
questions.correctAnswer: The program follows instructions in sequence
questions.explanation: Computers run instructions in the arranged order unless the program uses events, loops, or conditions.
questions.learningOutcome: Explore features of visual programming applications.

questions.prompt: Which visual programming block repeats an instruction several times?
questions.correctAnswer: Loop block
questions.explanation: A loop repeats selected instructions, which saves time and reduces repeated blocks.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify features used to create instructions in visual programming.

questions.prompt: A sprite starts moving only when the green flag is clicked. Which programming idea is shown?
questions.correctAnswer: Event
questions.explanation: An event is an action such as a click or key press that starts a set of instructions.
questions.learningOutcome: Explore event features in visual programming applications.

questions.prompt: A learner's animation should move 10 steps but moves 100 steps. What should the learner check first?
options: The value entered in the movement block
The colour of the classroom wall
The price of the computer table
The shape of a ceramic cup
questions.correctAnswer: The value entered in the movement block
questions.explanation: Debugging starts by checking the instruction likely causing the wrong output.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply debugging when creating instructions to solve problems.

questions.prompt: Which block would help a simple quiz program respond differently to right and wrong answers?
questions.correctAnswer: If-then-else condition block
questions.explanation: A condition lets a program choose one action when a test is true and another when it is false.
questions.learningOutcome: Create instructions to solve problems using visual programming applications.

questions.prompt: A visual program has start, repeat, move, check edge, and turn blocks. What problem is it likely solving?
options: Keeping an object moving inside the screen area
questions.correctAnswer: Keeping an object moving inside the screen area
questions.explanation: The blocks describe an animation that repeats movement and changes direction at the screen edge.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how visual programming instructions solve simple problems.

questions.prompt: A class wants a visual program that teaches fire safety. Which design plan is strongest?
options: Use scenes, question blocks, feedback, scoring, and restart instructions
Use one blank screen with no instructions
Hide every button so learners cannot interact
Add random blocks without testing the program
questions.correctAnswer: Use scenes, question blocks, feedback, scoring, and restart instructions
questions.explanation: A useful program has clear steps, interaction, feedback, and testing so users can learn from it.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a visual programming plan to solve a learning problem.

questions.prompt: What is a composite material?
options: A material made by combining two or more materials to improve properties
A material made only by counting money
A pure liquid used only for painting
A computer file with no content
questions.correctAnswer: A material made by combining two or more materials to improve properties
questions.explanation: Composite materials combine different materials so the final product has useful properties.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe composite materials used in production.

questions.prompt: Which item is an example of a composite material?
questions.correctAnswer: Plywood
questions.explanation: Plywood is made from layers of wood veneer glued together, making it a composite material.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify examples of composite materials in day-to-day use.

questions.prompt: Why are layers in plywood arranged and glued together?
options: To improve strength and reduce splitting compared with thin single boards
To make the wood dissolve in water
To remove all need for cutting tools
questions.correctAnswer: To improve strength and reduce splitting compared with thin single boards
questions.explanation: Layering wood in plywood improves stability and strength for many production tasks.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why composite materials are used in production.

questions.prompt: A group wants a light but stiff material for a small model bridge deck. Which choice is most suitable?
questions.correctAnswer: Thin plywood
questions.explanation: Thin plywood is light, stiff, and easier to cut for models than loose or wet materials.
questions.learningOutcome: Select composite materials for simple production tasks.

questions.prompt: Which comparison best shows an advantage and a limitation of some composite materials?
options: They can be strong and light, but may be harder to recycle
They are always free and never need tools
They are weaker than air and cannot be shaped
They are used only for writing passwords
questions.correctAnswer: They can be strong and light, but may be harder to recycle
questions.explanation: Composite materials often improve performance, but separating their parts for recycling can be difficult.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse advantages and limitations of composite materials.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to reduce waste when using offcuts of plywood. Which action is best?
options: Plan small products that match the offcut sizes before cutting
Throw away all offcuts without checking them
Cut random shapes until the sheet is finished
Soak every offcut in water overnight
questions.correctAnswer: Plan small products that match the offcut sizes before cutting
questions.explanation: Planning products around available offcuts conserves materials and supports responsible production.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse responsible use of composite materials in production.

questions.prompt: Which product plan best uses composite material properties?
options: A pencil holder from plywood with measured parts, safe joints, and smooth edges
A pencil holder from unmeasured wet soil with no drying plan
A shelf from loose paper stacked without glue
A signboard with no dimensions or material list
questions.correctAnswer: A pencil holder from plywood with measured parts, safe joints, and smooth edges
questions.explanation: A strong product plan matches material properties with measurements, joining, safety, and finishing.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a simple production plan using composite materials.

questions.prompt: Which material is commonly used to make ceramic products?
questions.correctAnswer: Clay
questions.explanation: Clay can be shaped, dried, and fired to make many ceramic products.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify materials used to make ceramic products.

questions.prompt: Which product is usually ceramic?
questions.correctAnswer: Clay cup
questions.explanation: A clay cup is a ceramic product because it is shaped from clay and hardened by drying and firing.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify ceramic products in the environment.

questions.prompt: Which property explains why ceramic tiles are useful near heat?
options: They can resist heat better than many plastics
They are always soft like cloth
They dissolve instantly in clean water
questions.correctAnswer: They can resist heat better than many plastics
questions.explanation: Many ceramics are hard and heat resistant, which makes them useful for tiles, cups, and cooking items.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe properties of ceramic materials.

questions.prompt: Why should a clay item dry slowly before firing?
options: To reduce cracking caused by trapped moisture
To remove the need for shaping
questions.correctAnswer: To reduce cracking caused by trapped moisture
questions.explanation: Slow drying lets moisture leave evenly, reducing cracks when the item is later fired.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain safe preparation steps when making ceramic products.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of glazing some ceramic products?
options: To give a smoother, less porous surface
To make the clay unfired again
To turn the product into sawdust
To remove all colour from the item
questions.correctAnswer: To give a smoother, less porous surface
questions.explanation: Glazing can improve appearance and make the ceramic surface easier to clean.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain finishing methods used on ceramic products.

questions.prompt: A learner finds a cracked ceramic plate in a practical area. What should the learner do?
options: Report it and handle it carefully to avoid cuts
Break it into smaller sharp pieces
Use it to scrape a power cable
questions.correctAnswer: Report it and handle it carefully to avoid cuts
questions.explanation: Cracked ceramics can have sharp edges, so they should be handled carefully and reported.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe handling practices for ceramic materials and products.

questions.prompt: Which reason best explains why ceramics may not be suitable for a dropped hand tool handle?
options: Ceramics can be brittle and may break under impact
Ceramics are always liquid at room temperature
questions.correctAnswer: Ceramics can be brittle and may break under impact
questions.explanation: Although ceramics can be hard and heat resistant, many are brittle and can crack or break when dropped.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse suitability of ceramic materials for different uses.

questions.prompt: Which cutting tool is suitable for cutting thin sheet metal?
questions.correctAnswer: Snips
questions.explanation: Snips are designed for cutting thin sheet metal safely and accurately when used correctly.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify cutting tools used for different materials.

questions.prompt: Which tool is commonly used to cut metal rods or pipes?
questions.correctAnswer: Hacksaw
questions.explanation: A hacksaw has a fine-toothed blade suitable for cutting metals and some plastics.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify cutting tools used for metalwork tasks.

questions.prompt: Which tool is best for cutting timber along a marked straight line?
questions.correctAnswer: Hand saw
questions.explanation: A hand saw cuts timber by moving its toothed blade along the marked line.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify cutting tools used for woodwork tasks.

questions.prompt: What is the main use of a chisel in production work?
options: Cutting or shaping wood with controlled blows or pressure
questions.correctAnswer: Cutting or shaping wood with controlled blows or pressure
questions.explanation: A chisel is used to cut, pare, or shape wood when guided safely.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the uses of common cutting tools.

questions.prompt: Why might a knife be safer than scissors for opening a thick carton under supervision?
options: A suitable knife can cut thick cardboard with less bending of the tool
A knife should be used without any control
Scissors are used only for computer files
A knife removes the need for a cutting surface
questions.correctAnswer: A suitable knife can cut thick cardboard with less bending of the tool
questions.explanation: Choosing a tool that matches the material reduces force, slipping, and tool damage when used safely.
questions.learningOutcome: Select cutting tools according to material and task.

questions.prompt: Why should material be clamped before sawing when possible?
options: Clamping holds the material steady and reduces slipping
questions.correctAnswer: Clamping holds the material steady and reduces slipping
questions.explanation: A steady workpiece improves accuracy and lowers the risk of injury while cutting.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain safety practices when using cutting tools.

questions.prompt: Which action is safest when passing a sharp cutting tool to another learner?
options: Pass it handle first after getting the person's attention
Hide it inside a pile of papers
questions.correctAnswer: Pass it handle first after getting the person's attention
questions.explanation: Passing a sharp tool handle first and communicating clearly helps prevent cuts and surprises.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe handling practices for cutting tools.

questions.prompt: A learner must cut plastic pipe and thin cardboard during one project. What should guide tool choice?
options: Material type, thickness, safety, and required finish
The brightest colour of the handle only
The tool nearest to the door
The tool with the longest name
questions.correctAnswer: Material type, thickness, safety, and required finish
questions.explanation: Tool selection should match the material, task, safety needs, and quality of the cut required.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse factors considered when selecting cutting tools.

questions.prompt: Which sequence is best for cutting a small plywood part accurately?
options: Measure, mark, clamp, cut, and smooth the edge
Cut first, guess later, and throw away the drawing
Paint the sheet before measuring anything
Start with smoothing and ignore the cutting line
questions.correctAnswer: Measure, mark, clamp, cut, and smooth the edge
questions.explanation: Accurate cutting follows a planned sequence from measurement to finishing.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe and accurate cutting procedures in production.

questions.prompt: A saw needs excessive force and leaves rough, torn edges. What is the most likely issue?
options: The blade may be blunt or unsuitable for the material
The material has already been fully finished
The drawing title block is too large
questions.correctAnswer: The blade may be blunt or unsuitable for the material
questions.explanation: A blunt or wrong blade can make cutting unsafe, slow, and inaccurate.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse cutting problems and choose safe corrective action.

questions.prompt: What is computer software?
options: Programs and instructions that tell a computer what to do
Only the metal case around a computer
A hand tool for cutting timber
A ceramic material fired in a kiln
questions.correctAnswer: Programs and instructions that tell a computer what to do
questions.explanation: Software is the set of programs and instructions that make computer hardware perform tasks.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the meaning of computer software.

questions.prompt: Which software helps manage computer hardware and allows other programs to run?
questions.correctAnswer: Operating system
questions.explanation: An operating system manages hardware, files, memory, and other software on a computer.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify types of computer software and their functions.

questions.prompt: Which software would be most suitable for typing a report about a production project?
questions.correctAnswer: Word processor
questions.explanation: A word processor is application software used to type, edit, and format text documents.
questions.learningOutcome: Select application software for a given task.

questions.prompt: Which file-management practice helps a learner find project files quickly?
options: Use clear file names and organised folders
Store files only in the recycle bin
questions.correctAnswer: Use clear file names and organised folders
questions.explanation: Clear names and folders make it easier to store, retrieve, and share digital work responsibly.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply software file-management features in project work.

questions.prompt: A class wants to total costs for wood, glue, and nails. Which software is most useful?
questions.correctAnswer: Spreadsheet
questions.explanation: A spreadsheet can organise numbers and use formulas to calculate totals, costs, and budgets.
questions.learningOutcome: Use software tools to support simple production calculations.

questions.prompt: Which action is safest before installing unfamiliar software on a school computer?
options: Ask the teacher and confirm the source is trusted
Install it quickly from any pop-up advert
Share the administrator password with friends
questions.correctAnswer: Ask the teacher and confirm the source is trusted
questions.explanation: Software from untrusted sources can contain malware or violate school rules.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe practices when using and installing software.

questions.prompt: A group needs a poster for marketing and a table for product costs. Which software combination is best?
options: Presentation or design software for the poster and spreadsheet software for costs
Antivirus only for both poster and cost table
Calculator only for drawing all graphics
Operating system settings only for both tasks
questions.correctAnswer: Presentation or design software for the poster and spreadsheet software for costs
questions.explanation: Different software is chosen according to the task: design tools for visuals and spreadsheets for calculations.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse software choices for production and business tasks.

questions.prompt: What is bookkeeping?
options: Recording business financial transactions in an organised way
Firing clay products in a kiln
questions.correctAnswer: Recording business financial transactions in an organised way
questions.explanation: Bookkeeping keeps records of money coming in, money going out, debts, assets, and other transactions.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the meaning of bookkeeping.

questions.prompt: Which item is an asset for a small school business club?
options: A sewing machine owned by the club
A promise to repay a loan
questions.correctAnswer: A sewing machine owned by the club
questions.explanation: An asset is something valuable owned by a business, such as cash, stock, tools, or equipment.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify basic bookkeeping terms used in business.

questions.prompt: Which example is a liability?
options: Money a business owes for materials bought on credit
Cash kept in the business box
A display table owned by the business
questions.correctAnswer: Money a business owes for materials bought on credit
questions.explanation: A liability is an amount owed by a business to another person or organisation.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify assets, liabilities, and capital in bookkeeping.

questions.prompt: Which equation correctly shows the relationship among assets, liabilities, and capital?
questions.correctAnswer: Assets = Liabilities + Capital
questions.explanation: The bookkeeping equation shows that business assets are financed by liabilities and owner's capital.
questions.learningOutcome: Use the bookkeeping equation to relate assets, liabilities, and capital.

questions.prompt: A business has liabilities of KES 4,000 and capital of KES 6,000. What are its assets?
questions.explanation: Assets equal liabilities plus capital, so 4,000 + 6,000 = 10,000.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate assets using the bookkeeping equation.

questions.prompt: A customer takes a product and promises to pay next week. How should this transaction be classified?
questions.correctAnswer: Credit sale
questions.explanation: A credit sale occurs when goods or services are given now and payment is expected later.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify cash and credit transactions in bookkeeping.

questions.prompt: A club makes a bag for KES 1,600 and sells it for KES 2,000. What is the profit?
questions.correctAnswer: KES 400
questions.explanation: Profit is selling price minus cost price, so 2,000 - 1,600 = 400.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate profit and loss from cost and selling price.

questions.prompt: Which statement shows the financial position of a business at a particular date?
questions.correctAnswer: Statement of financial position
questions.explanation: A statement of financial position shows assets, liabilities, and capital at a specific date.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify components of a statement of financial position.

questions.prompt: What does a cash flow statement mainly show?
options: Cash inflows and cash outflows over a period
Only the sizes on a drawing
Only the names of cutting tools
questions.correctAnswer: Cash inflows and cash outflows over a period
questions.explanation: A cash flow statement tracks how cash enters and leaves a business during a period.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the components and purpose of a cash flow statement.

questions.prompt: A business has sales of KES 12,000 and total expenses of KES 8,500 for a period. What result should its income statement show?
questions.correctAnswer: Profit of KES 3,500
questions.explanation: Profit is income minus expenses, so 12,000 - 8,500 = 3,500.
questions.learningOutcome: Prepare simple income statement calculations for a business.

questions.prompt: Which is a source of income for an individual learner during a supervised school project?
options: Earning money from selling approved handmade bookmarks
questions.correctAnswer: Earning money from selling approved handmade bookmarks
questions.explanation: Income is money received, such as earnings from selling goods or providing a service.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify sources of income for an individual.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of a personal budget?
options: To plan income, spending, and saving
questions.correctAnswer: To plan income, spending, and saving
questions.explanation: A budget helps a person decide how to use available money responsibly.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of budgeting in day-to-day life.

questions.prompt: A learner receives KES 600 and plans KES 250 for materials, KES 150 for transport, and KES 100 for savings. How much remains unallocated?
questions.correctAnswer: KES 100
questions.explanation: Planned use is 250 + 150 + 100 = 500, so 600 - 500 = 100 remains.
questions.learningOutcome: Prepare simple budget calculations for personal financial management.

questions.prompt: Which budgeting practice is ethical?
options: Recording expected income and expenses honestly
Hiding some expenses from group members
Using project money for personal snacks without permission
questions.correctAnswer: Recording expected income and expenses honestly
questions.explanation: Ethical budgeting requires honesty, transparency, and responsible use of money.
questions.learningOutcome: Explore ethical and unethical practices in income and budgeting.

questions.prompt: Which choice shows wise spending for a learner preparing a project?
options: Compare prices, buy needed materials first, and keep receipts
Buy decorations before checking required materials
Spend all income before listing needs
questions.correctAnswer: Compare prices, buy needed materials first, and keep receipts
questions.explanation: Wise spending prioritises needs, compares costs, and keeps evidence for accurate records.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain responsible spending practices in personal budgeting.

questions.prompt: A learner's material cost rises from KES 300 to KES 420, but income remains KES 700. What is the best budget decision?
options: Revise the budget and reduce lower-priority spending
Ignore the extra cost and spend as before
Remove savings without checking other choices
questions.correctAnswer: Revise the budget and reduce lower-priority spending
questions.explanation: A budget should be reviewed when costs change so that essential needs are still covered.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse budget adjustments when income or expenses change.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to save KES 900 in nine weeks for a drawing set. Which plan is best?
options: Save KES 100 each week and record progress
Save only when extra money appears by chance
Spend first and write records later
Borrow the full amount without a repayment plan
questions.correctAnswer: Save KES 100 each week and record progress
questions.explanation: A measurable savings plan states the amount, time, and method for tracking progress.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a simple financial plan for income management.

questions.prompt: Why is marketing important to a small business?
options: It helps customers learn about goods and services
It removes the need for records
questions.correctAnswer: It helps customers learn about goods and services
questions.explanation: Marketing communicates value to customers and helps a business connect products with needs.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of marketing to a business.

questions.prompt: Which method can help learners find information about potential customers for a school-made product?
options: Asking target users simple survey questions
Hiding the product until sale day
questions.correctAnswer: Asking target users simple survey questions
questions.explanation: A survey can reveal customer needs, preferred prices, and useful product features.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse sources of information about the market and potential customers.

questions.prompt: A group wants to sell pencil holders near the school exhibition. Which factor should they consider when selecting the market?
options: Whether visitors need and can afford the product
Whether the sellers can avoid explaining the product
Whether there is no place to display items
Whether the price is hidden from customers
questions.correctAnswer: Whether visitors need and can afford the product
questions.explanation: A suitable market has potential customers with need, interest, access, and ability to pay.
questions.learningOutcome: Explore factors considered when selecting a suitable market for goods and services.

questions.prompt: Which ICT tool can be used responsibly to market goods during a school-approved project?
options: A teacher-approved digital poster or notice
A secret message that hides the price
A copied advert with false claims
questions.correctAnswer: A teacher-approved digital poster or notice
questions.explanation: Responsible ICT marketing uses approved channels, truthful information, and safe digital behaviour.
questions.learningOutcome: Select tools to market goods and services.

questions.prompt: Which marketing message is most ethical for handmade notebooks?
options: Made from neat recycled paper; sizes and prices are shown clearly
Guaranteed to last forever even if not tested
Only clever learners may buy this product
The price will be decided after payment
questions.correctAnswer: Made from neat recycled paper; sizes and prices are shown clearly
questions.explanation: Ethical marketing is truthful, respectful, and clear about product features and price.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse ethical communication when marketing goods and services.

questions.prompt: What is the role of an intermediary in distribution?
options: To help move goods or services from producers to consumers
questions.correctAnswer: To help move goods or services from producers to consumers
questions.explanation: Intermediaries such as wholesalers and retailers help goods reach customers more efficiently.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of intermediaries in distribution.

questions.prompt: Which sequence shows a common channel of distribution for goods?
options: Producer, waste bin, title block, loop
questions.correctAnswer: Producer, wholesaler, retailer, consumer
questions.explanation: Many goods move from producers through wholesalers and retailers before reaching consumers.
questions.learningOutcome: Illustrate channels for distributing goods and services in business.

questions.prompt: A group sells fresh juice during a school event. Which distribution choice is most suitable?
options: Sell directly at a clean stand near the customers
Send it through many delays before serving
Store it in direct sun all day
Hide it far from the event entrance
questions.correctAnswer: Sell directly at a clean stand near the customers
questions.explanation: Fresh products need a short, hygienic distribution channel so they reach customers quickly and safely.
questions.learningOutcome: Select suitable distribution channels for different goods and services.

questions.prompt: Which practice is unethical in the distribution of goods?
options: Changing package labels to hide expired products
Delivering goods safely and on time
questions.correctAnswer: Changing package labels to hide expired products
questions.explanation: Changing labels to mislead customers is dishonest and can expose people to unsafe products.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse ethical issues in distribution of goods and services.

questions.prompt: A club must distribute 40 desk organisers to buyers in three classrooms. Which plan is best?
options: List buyers, group deliveries by classroom, check each item, and record payments
Carry all items randomly and hope buyers find them
Deliver before checking names or quantities
Give items only to friends without records
questions.correctAnswer: List buyers, group deliveries by classroom, check each item, and record payments
questions.explanation: A strong distribution plan uses records, grouping, quality checks, and fair delivery to customers.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a simple ethical distribution plan for goods and services.
